advanced_settings.name: Advanced settings
advanced_settings.description: Optional source mappings, attributes, event hooks, command actions, and integration-specific settings.

data_description.template_sources_json:
Maps Jinja variable names to source states or attributes. YAML example:
source: sensor.room_temperature
battery: sensor.remote.battery_level
Use variables named source and battery in editable templates.
Multiple sources:
source: sensor.room_temperature
battery: sensor.remote.battery_level
Then reference the variables from value_template.
data_description.event_hooks_json:
Runs editable helpers after a state or event trigger. YAML example:
- trigger: state
  entity_id: [sensor.source]
  value_template: trigger.to_state.state  # wrap in Jinja delimiters
Hooks may also set availability_template, attributes, and attribute_templates.
data_description.attributes_json:
Static extra attributes published by the virtual entity. YAML example:
source_type: composite
priority: 1
data_description.attribute_sources_json:
Maps a virtual attribute to a real entity state or attribute. YAML example:
battery: sensor.remote.battery_level
mode: select.real_mode.state
data_description.attribute_templates_json:
Maps attributes to editable Jinja helpers. YAML example:
power: states("sensor.power") | float(0)  # wrap this expression in Jinja delimiters
Automatic helpers use boolean AND/OR, numeric average, unique list union, string concatenation, or ordered mapping merge according to value type.
data_description.native_templates_json:
Maps native Home Assistant properties to Jinja. YAML example:
vendor_property: state_attr("sensor.source", "vendor_property")  # wrap in Jinja delimiters
Managed properties are normally shown individually in Native values; this editor keeps additional domain/vendor properties editable.
data_description.command_actions_json:
Maps every virtual-domain command to Home Assistant actions. Command arguments such as preset_mode, percentage, temperature, option, or position are template variables. YAML example:
set_preset_mode:
  - choose:
      - conditions: preset_mode == "sleep"  # wrap in Jinja delimiters
        sequence:
          - action: input_select.select_option
            target:
              entity_id: input_select.real_mode
            data:
              option: quiet
A value may be one action, an action list, or a mapping with sequence and optimistic keys.
More examples:
turn_on:
  - action: switch.turn_on
    target:
      entity_id: switch.real_device
set_percentage:
  - action: number.set_value
    target:
      entity_id: number.fan_speed
    data:
      value: percentage # command variable; wrap expressions in Jinja delimiters
data_description.domain_options_json:
Additional selected-domain options not represented by dedicated inputs. YAML example:
source_entity: camera.front_door
stream_source: rtsp://example/stream
Reserved common fields cannot be overridden.
Climate example:
hvac_modes: select.climate_modes
current_temperature: sensor.room_temperature
Fan example:
preset_modes: select.fan_modes
Use dedicated Native values for standard properties when available.

entity_source.title: Copy From Existing Entities
entity_source.description: Optionally choose one or more Home Assistant entities. Multiple sources generate starter templates automatically.

data_description.reference_entity_id: Leave empty to create a virtual entity from scratch. Boolean sources use AND, motion/presence sources use majority with delayed clear, safety sources such as leak, smoke, gas, and water use OR, numeric sources use average, text sources use concat, date/time sources use latest, select sources use first available, and multiple location sources use median GPS with recent outlier priority (300 m for 30 minutes). A heating-only climate source is simplified to heat/off. Selecting exactly one climate and one switch creates a boiler helper: the hot-water switch remains on in both modes, heat uses the climate heat mode, and virtual off uses the climate fan-only mode. Camera and image sources can be aliased one at a time, not merged.

advanced_settings.description: Optional source mappings, attributes, event hooks, command actions, and integration-specific settings.

data_description.template_sources_json:
Maps Jinja variable names to source states or attributes. YAML example:
source: sensor.room_temperature
battery: sensor.remote.battery_level
Use variables named source and battery in editable templates.
Multiple sources:
source: sensor.room_temperature
battery: sensor.remote.battery_level
Then reference the variables from value_template.
data_description.event_hooks_json:
Runs editable helpers after a state or event trigger. YAML example:
- trigger: state
  entity_id: [sensor.source]
  value_template: trigger.to_state.state  # wrap in Jinja delimiters
Hooks may also set availability_template, attributes, and attribute_templates.
data_description.attributes_json:
Static extra attributes published by the virtual entity. YAML example:
source_type: composite
priority: 1
data_description.attribute_sources_json:
Maps a virtual attribute to a real entity state or attribute. YAML example:
battery: sensor.remote.battery_level
mode: select.real_mode.state
data_description.attribute_templates_json:
Maps attributes to editable Jinja helpers. YAML example:
power: states("sensor.power") | float(0)  # wrap this expression in Jinja delimiters
Automatic helpers use boolean AND/OR, numeric average, unique list union, string concatenation, or ordered mapping merge according to value type.
data_description.native_templates_json:
Maps native Home Assistant properties to Jinja. YAML example:
vendor_property: state_attr("sensor.source", "vendor_property")  # wrap in Jinja delimiters
Managed properties are normally shown individually in Native values; this editor keeps additional domain/vendor properties editable.
data_description.command_actions_json:
Maps every virtual-domain command to Home Assistant actions. Command arguments such as preset_mode, percentage, temperature, option, or position are template variables. YAML example:
set_preset_mode:
  - choose:
      - conditions: preset_mode == "sleep"  # wrap in Jinja delimiters
        sequence:
          - action: input_select.select_option
            target:
              entity_id: input_select.real_mode
            data:
              option: quiet
A value may be one action, an action list, or a mapping with sequence and optimistic keys.
More examples:
turn_on:
  - action: switch.turn_on
    target:
      entity_id: switch.real_device
set_percentage:
  - action: number.set_value
    target:
      entity_id: number.fan_speed
    data:
      value: percentage # command variable; wrap expressions in Jinja delimiters
data_description.domain_options_json:
Additional selected-domain options not represented by dedicated inputs. YAML example:
source_entity: camera.front_door
stream_source: rtsp://example/stream
Reserved common fields cannot be overridden.
Climate example:
hvac_modes: select.climate_modes
current_temperature: sensor.room_temperature
Fan example:
preset_modes: select.fan_modes
Use dedicated Native values for standard properties when available.

data_description.reference_entity_id: Leave empty to keep the current virtual entity values. Boolean sources use AND, motion/presence sources use majority with delayed clear, safety sources such as leak, smoke, gas, and water use OR, numeric sources use average, text sources use concat, date/time sources use latest, select sources use first available, and multiple location sources use median GPS with recent outlier priority (300 m for 30 minutes). A heating-only climate source is simplified to heat/off. Selecting exactly one climate and one switch creates a boiler helper: the hot-water switch remains on in both modes, heat uses the climate heat mode, and virtual off uses the climate fan-only mode. Camera and image sources can be aliased one at a time, not merged.

advanced_settings.description: Optional source mappings, attributes, event hooks, command actions, and integration-specific settings.

data_description.template_sources_json:
Maps Jinja variable names to source states or attributes. YAML example:
source: sensor.room_temperature
battery: sensor.remote.battery_level
Use variables named source and battery in editable templates.
Multiple sources:
source: sensor.room_temperature
battery: sensor.remote.battery_level
Then reference the variables from value_template.
data_description.event_hooks_json:
Runs editable helpers after a state or event trigger. YAML example:
- trigger: state
  entity_id: [sensor.source]
  value_template: trigger.to_state.state  # wrap in Jinja delimiters
Hooks may also set availability_template, attributes, and attribute_templates.
data_description.attributes_json:
Static extra attributes published by the virtual entity. YAML example:
source_type: composite
priority: 1
data_description.attribute_sources_json:
Maps a virtual attribute to a real entity state or attribute. YAML example:
battery: sensor.remote.battery_level
mode: select.real_mode.state
data_description.attribute_templates_json:
Maps attributes to editable Jinja helpers. YAML example:
power: states("sensor.power") | float(0)  # wrap this expression in Jinja delimiters
Automatic helpers use boolean AND/OR, numeric average, unique list union, string concatenation, or ordered mapping merge according to value type.
data_description.native_templates_json:
Maps native Home Assistant properties to Jinja. YAML example:
vendor_property: state_attr("sensor.source", "vendor_property")  # wrap in Jinja delimiters
Managed properties are normally shown individually in Native values; this editor keeps additional domain/vendor properties editable.
data_description.command_actions_json:
Maps every virtual-domain command to Home Assistant actions. Command arguments such as preset_mode, percentage, temperature, option, or position are template variables. YAML example:
set_preset_mode:
  - choose:
      - conditions: preset_mode == "sleep"  # wrap in Jinja delimiters
        sequence:
          - action: input_select.select_option
            target:
              entity_id: input_select.real_mode
            data:
              option: quiet
A value may be one action, an action list, or a mapping with sequence and optimistic keys.
More examples:
turn_on:
  - action: switch.turn_on
    target:
      entity_id: switch.real_device
set_percentage:
  - action: number.set_value
    target:
      entity_id: number.fan_speed
    data:
      value: percentage # command variable; wrap expressions in Jinja delimiters
data_description.domain_options_json:
Additional selected-domain options not represented by dedicated inputs. YAML example:
source_entity: camera.front_door
stream_source: rtsp://example/stream
Reserved common fields cannot be overridden.
Climate example:
hvac_modes: select.climate_modes
current_temperature: sensor.room_temperature
Fan example:
preset_modes: select.fan_modes
Use dedicated Native values for standard properties when available.

entity_source.title: Copy From Existing Entities
entity_source.description: Optionally choose one or more Home Assistant entities. Multiple sources generate starter templates automatically.

data_description.reference_entity_id: Leave empty to create a virtual entity from scratch. Boolean sources use AND, motion/presence sources use majority with delayed clear, safety sources such as leak, smoke, gas, and water use OR, numeric sources use average, text sources use concat, date/time sources use latest, select sources use first available, and multiple location sources use median GPS with recent outlier priority (300 m for 30 minutes). A heating-only climate source is simplified to heat/off. Selecting exactly one climate and one switch creates a boiler helper: the hot-water switch remains on in both modes, heat uses the climate heat mode, and virtual off uses the climate fan-only mode. Camera and image sources can be aliased one at a time, not merged.
